1 The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of Selvi in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2.That on 19.9.2023 at about 7.15 p.m., Selvi was an occupant in BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-1385, when she was getting down from the bus on Old Madras Road, at RMZ Mallenia bus stop, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the bus suddenly moved the bus.
Due to the tremendous impact Selvi was fell down from the bus and sustained multiple injuries.

Immediately she was shifted to CVR hospital,
Benglauru, again she was shifted to Manipal hospital, further shifted to M.S.
Ramaiah Hospital, Benglauru.
She was discharged from the hospital on 23.9.2023 with an advice to continue her treatment.
3. The petitioner further stated that, due to the complications of head injuries, Selvi was died on her way to Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bengaluru on 23.9.2023.

entities.text: Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Thereafter post mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners.
Subsequently, obsequies and funeral ceremonies of the deceased was performed by spending huge amount.

4. It is further stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, and was aged about 54 years and house maid and earning Rs.30,000/-
per month.
Due to the unnatural death of the deceased, the petitioners' life become dark, miserable and depressed and put to great financial hardship.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred, due to the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle, BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-1385.
In this regard, criminal case was registered against him, in Crime No.153/2023, for the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of I.P.C, by the jurisdictional police.
As such, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Hence, the petitioners have approached this court, seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/-
consequent upon the death of Selvi in the alleged accident.
6. After service of the notice of this petition, respondent has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement in answer to the case of the petitioners.

7. In the written statement of the respondent, not seriously disputed the accident and the death of Selvi, denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Further, denied the manner of the accident, age, occupation and income of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.

With all these main grounds,
prayed to dismiss the petition against the respondent.

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that Selvi had died due to the injuries sustained by her in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on on 19.9.2023 at about 7.15 p.m., Old Madras road, at RMZ Mellenia bus stop, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-1385 in an actionable negligence ?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3) What order or award?

Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:-
18.
It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC bus bearing No.KA-57-F-1385, the alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Smt.Selvi had died in the said accident.
As such, the petitioners have filed this claim petition against the respondents.
19. On the contrary, the respondent though not disputed the accident and the death of Selvi, but strongly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC bus.
In such a situation, burden is more on the part of the petitioners, to prove the above issues on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
20. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 has examined as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
PW1 in support of her oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to Ex.P10
. Ex. P1-true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.153/2023 of Halasuru Traffic Police Station.
Ex.P2- true copy of first information statement given by Aravind, Ex.P3- true copy of requisition letter to inculcate Section 304(A) of IPC,

Ex.P4-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P5-true copy of sketch, Ex.P6-true copy of P.M. report,
Ex.P7-inquest report, Ex.P8-IMV report, Ex.P9-true copy of charge sheet and Ex.P10-police intimation.

21. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by Aravind, the S.H.O. of Halasuru Traffic police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
22.
On the contrary, driver of the BMTC bus bearing No.KA-57-F-1385 was examined as RW1.

He has strongly contended that, when he was going to stop in RMZ Millenia bus stop for alighting passenger, at that time deceased Selvi try to getting down from the moving bus hurriedly and negligently, at that time she was dashed door and lost the control and she was fallen from the bus and there is no negligence on his part.

24. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing No.KA- 57-F-1385 and in the said accident, Smt.Selvi succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2;
25.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P11 to Ex.P13 and Ex.P16 & Ex.P17 Aadhar cards of the petitioners and deceased and Birth certificates of petitioners, have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

26. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the age particulars of the petitioners, mentioned in the cause title of the petition, reflected that, the petitioner No.1 & 2 being the major daughters of the deceased have lost the love and affection of their mother in the family.
The respondents herein have not produced documents on record, to show the independent economic status of the petitioners.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents to the deceased during his lifetime.
27. In the case on hand, no doubt the major daughters of deceased Selvi filed this claim petition.
According to them, they were dependents to the deceased petitioner during her lifetime.
No contra materials are available on record to show that, they were not dependents to their mother during her lifetime.
Hence, it is necessary to discuss the point that, mother played an important role in the family or not.
All the children, one or the other way defendants to their mother whether they are minors or majors, married or unmarried.
During the minority of the child, dependency is more on the mother.
After the marriage of the daughters, the percentage of dependency is less on mother, if compare with the minor children.

28. In the case on hand, by looking to the age criteria though they are major daughters, they could have dependents to their mother not only economically, but, in connection with love and affection and also with respect to domestic work of Selvi during her lifetime.

Hence, the petitioners can be presumed as dependents to their mother during her lifetime in the absence of contra materials from Anitha N vs B.M.T.C on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89359299/
5
the other side.

At this stage, the counsel for the petitioners has relied the decision of the Hon'bel Supreme Court, in National Insurance Company Lilmited V/S Birender and Others stated that, a major and earning son has a right to claim compensation under Motor Vehicle Act.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Lilmited V/S Birender and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, by referring the case of Manjuri Bera, stated that, even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant if he was a legal representative will be entitled to compensation.

Even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation, and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application, irrespective of the fact, whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."
29.

The petitioners herein, to prove the actual age of the deceased, as on the date of the accident,
have placed Aadhar card as per Ex.P13.
On perusal of Aadhar card marked at Ex.P13, the date of the deceased Selvi has been mentioned as 8.3.1967.
The alleged accident was occurred on 19..9.2023.
The said document remained unquestioned by the other side.
Hence, it is apt to consider that, as on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged about 56 years.
For her age, multiplier '9' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.

30. In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition, and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was working as a house maid and used to earn income of Rs.30,000/- per month.
But in support of definite income of the deceased, there is no iota of documents.
In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken into consideration.
Hence, the income of the deceased is apt to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m., which will meet the ends of justice.
31. Another point to be taken in to consideration herein that, as per the petition, two persons were depending on the earning of the deceased.
In this regard, about the deduction of the personal and living expenses is concerned, the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14 is to be considered.

32. Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others,
"

entities.text: 2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "

6 33.

Having considered the above as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependant family members exceeds six."
In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.

In the present case,
deceased was aged about 56 years, as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "9" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such by taking into consideration of the self-employment mentioned in the petition, I am of the view that, 10% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,000/- per month. And Rs.1,92,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 10% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,92,000+19,200) = Rs.2,11,200/-.

And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living e x p e n s e s i n t h e i n c o m e o f t h e d e c e a s e d . T h u s , n e t l o s s i n c o m e c o m e s t o Rs.1,40,800/-(Rs.2,11,200-Rs.70,400).This
income has to be multiplied by multiplier "9".
Which comes to Rs.12,67,200/-.

34. Apart from this, aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium, and with respect to the funeral expenses, to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.
National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

35. Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Medical expenses:
37.
After the accident deceased was admitted to various hospitals and petitioners have spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
The petitioners have placed discharge summary as per Ex.P14 issued by M.S. Ramaiah Hospital and medical bills at ex.P15 to the extent of Rs.3,94,791/-.

Further placed medical bill for Rs.60,000/-
at Ex.P18, payment receipt at Ex.P19 and discharge summary of Manipal Hospital at Ex.P20.
On perusal of medical bills it is clear that the petitioners have spent Rs.4,54,791/-.
Though the respondent has disputed the medical bills but not placed any contra materials to show that the medical bills are created.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.4,54,791/- towards medical expenses.
38. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.
Compensation heads Compensation  Amount

Towards loss of Rs.12,67,200-00  dependency  Towards loss of Rs. 88,000-00  consortium  Towards loss of estate Rs. 16,500-00  Towards funeral & Rs. 16,500-00  obsequies ceremony  expenses  Medical expenses Rs. 4,54,791-00  Total Rs.18,42,991-00 39.

sentences.text: As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle in the RTA, Selvi had succumbed to the injuries.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with this point, as fully discussed in Issue No.1, remained unshaken.
Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

In such a situation, the respondent being the owner cum internal insurance company of the offending vehicle BMTC bus No.KA-57-F-1385 is liable to pay the compensation determined by this court to the petitioners along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till its realization.
Resultantly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
41.

In view of my due discussions on point Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R  The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.18,42,991/- (Rupees eighteen lakh forty two thousand nine hundred and ninety one only) along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled the share of 30%, the petitioner No.2 is entitled the share of 70%.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 & 2, shall deposit 40% of their share in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to them through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
